To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the system is capable of transmitting neural signals from axons in cockroaches and forelimb of a rat, wirelessly, with high fidelity, over a distance of 22 ft.
we designed, fabricated and tested a 3-channel wireless microsystem which can record neural signals from axons in cockroaches and from the forelimb area (M1) of the motor cortex in rats.

we have successfully developed a small, lightweight, low-power, wireless multichannel neural recording system which has been successfully used to record neural signals from two very different animal models: cockroach and rat.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design and development of a low-power, low-noise, multichannel neural recording microsystem that can be used for long-term, in-vivo, chronic recordings of neural activity.
the development of a small, light-weight (including batteries), low power wireless multichannel neural recording system that is capable of long range data transmission.
the design, fabrication, and characterization of a small, light-weight (1cm3 and 1g, respectively), low-power, long-range (22 ft.), multichannel wireless microsystem for neural recording.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the system is able to perform as designed.
the system is capable of recording neural signals in-vitro as well as in-vivo.
a small, light-weight (<1 g), low-power (10 mW), long range (10m) wireless neural recording system has been successfully designed and fabricated.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a small, low-power, low-cost, multichannel, wireless neural recording system was designed, fabricated and tested in-vitro as well as in-vivo.
the microsystem can be employed in collecting neural activity from the cockroach and the rat.
the system has been designed to be a low power, long range wireless neural recording device.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we can record neural signals from multiple channels wirelessly and in a low power manner.
a small and light-weight, low power wireless neural recording system can be used to collect neural signals from different parts of the nervous system.
the wireless microsystem is able to collect and transmit high quality neural signals from the cockroach leg, and the rat motor cortex.
